pattern: refinanc\w*[^.]{0,60}house you are buying|house you are buying[^.]{0,80}refinanc
struck: Cash from refinancing the house you are buying cannot count as its reserves.
use: Cash taken out in a cash-out refinance cannot count toward the reserves for that same refinance.

pattern: (home|house) you live in,? and buy(ing)? another
struck: Renting out the home you live in and buying another: the lender counts three quarters of its market rent.
use: Renting out the home you live in when you buy a new home to live in: the lender counts three quarters of its market rent.

struck: Plus a share of what you owe on your other financed rentals.
use: Plus a share of what you owe on your other financed homes, not counting your own home and the new one.

pattern: HUD's rent[^.]{0,80}lender counts|lender counts about \$?1,6[67]\d of it
struck: HUD's rent for a 3-bedroom in that ZIP is $2,230 a month; the lender counts about $1,670 of it.
use: If the appraiser's rent schedule came in at $2,230, HUD's figure for a 3-bedroom in that ZIP, the lender would count about $1,670.

struck: Landlord insurance about $3,300 a year (one agency's estimate); about $767 a month, $9,200 a year.
use: (cut the insurance figure: tax and dues about $5,900 a year, about $492 a month; insurance is the reader's own quote)

struck: The standard rule asks you to keep about $10,100 plus six months of the new loan's principal and interest.
use: The standard rule asks you to keep about $8,400, plus six months of the new loan's payment and insurance.

struck: Both houses empty for three months: about $4,600 in tax, insurance and dues.
use: Both houses empty for three months: about $2,950 in tax and dues, plus three payments on each loan.

pattern: not the six loan payments|unless they are no larger
struck: It covers that three-month double vacancy's tax, insurance and dues with about $5,500 left, but not the six loan payments on two loans unless they are no larger than the new loan's six.
use: Three empty months on both houses take about $2,950 of that in tax and dues, plus three payments on each loan.

struck: A legal residence rented out more than 72 days in a year loses the 4 percent rate.
use: A legal residence rented out more than 72 days in a calendar year loses the 4 percent rate (active-duty military on orders keep it).

struck: 257 buyers recorded two or more Horry County home purchases: 126 people and 131 companies. Together they bought 650 homes. 193 of them bought exactly two.
use: 255 buyers recorded two or more Horry County home purchases: 138 people and 117 companies. Together they bought 645 homes. 192 of them bought exactly two.

struck: Half of those homes now send the tax bill outside South Carolina.
use: Of those homes the buyers still own, half send the tax bill outside South Carolina.

struck: 6,070 people and companies own two or more homes taxed at the 6 percent rate. 4,091 own exactly two. 3,563 of the 6,070 are people. They hold 23,290 homes.
use: About 6,000 people and companies own two or more homes taxed at the 6 percent rate, not counting resort and timeshare firms. About 4,100 own exactly two. About 4,200 are people, some through a family trust.

struck: Of 3,563 houses with 3 or more bedrooms for sale in Horry County, 67 ask $195,000 or less; of 1,897 condos with 2 or more bedrooms, 432 do.
use: Of 2,889 houses with 3 or more bedrooms for sale in Horry County, 9 ask $195,000 or less; of 1,756 condos with 2 or more bedrooms, 417 do.
